concept.name: Double-distribution day
concept.definition: A Market Profile day type in which the session forms two distinct value distributions separated by a column of single prints: after an initial balance and first rotation, longer-timeframe participants reprice the market to a new region, where a second balance forms and typically holds into the close. It is a structured form of trend day in which the market repriced mid-session.
concept.intuition: The market built one fair-value zone, decisively abandoned it, sprinted through a no-man's land of single prints, and built a second fair-value zone higher (or lower).
concept.mechanics: Identified on the profile as two TPO bulges joined by single-print rows; the first distribution forms around the initial balance, the second after the drive, and the separating singles mark the zone that was never accepted.
concept.failure_modes: Whether two bulges count as separate distributions is a judgment call sensitive to bracket size; the single-print separator is often filled in later sessions, erasing the structure that the classification relied on.
concept.misconceptions: The second distribution holding into the close does not guarantee continuation the next day; the pattern describes how the session repriced, not where the next one must go.
concept.example: Morning trade builds value around 4,500–4,510; at midday a drive runs through single prints at 4,512–4,516 and the afternoon builds a second distribution at 4,518–4,528 that holds into the close — a double-distribution day.
